subject: RapidCharge: integration recap + model routing policy rollout
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Collins <avery.collins@rapidcharge.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: RapidCharge discovery — integration recap & proposed next steps

Hi Avery / Samir —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick internal recap and the action plan we discussed so we’re all aligned. I’m copying the implementation owners on our side.

Summary of needs from RapidCharge:
- Real-time suggestion & reranking for customer service chat (low single-digit token latency objective).
- Embedding-based semantic search for KB + reranker for precision-sensitive flows (fraud detection).
- Must be deployable in us-west region initially; potential EU expansion in Q4.
- Compliance: SOC 2 + audit logs required; minimal PII retention for chat transcripts.

Constraints you mentioned:
- Hard latency SLO for primary chat path: p95 < 220ms.
- Cost sensitivity: preference for a routing policy that uses smaller quantized models for cheap bulk work and larger models for high-confidence answers.

Proposed technical approach (high level):
1) SDK + auth: we’ll provide a lightweight Node SDK sample and short-lived test credentials to integrate with your staging environment.
2) Model routing policy: default to a mid-sized quantized candidate (e.g., 8-bit Llama-variant) for initial token generation + a routing step to escalate to a larger full-precision model for low-confidence outputs (confidence threshold tunable).
3) Embeddings/reranker: run embedding index in your VPC (or our hosted embeddings with encrypted transit), with a candidate rerank step that calls a small cross-encoder reranker.
4) Fallback chain: primary -> quantized large -> hosted large (fallback to cross-region if capacity constrained).

Next steps we committed to on the call:
- Redwood: send SDK quickstart, test creds, and a draft SOW for review (today).
- RapidCharge: share current KB sample, expected traffic profile (RPS + avg tokens), and security questionnaire answers (by EOD Tue).
- Schedule an architecture workshop with infra + security (45m) next week.

Attachments: initial SOW draft + our risk matrix (stubs attached).

I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the workshop once you confirm availability.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0114

Thanks for the clear recap, Irene. A couple of asks from the sales side to keep momentum: 

- Can we get a short one-page pilot success criteria doc? I’ll use this in the buying committee to frame the pilot scope and KPIs (latency target, precision on reranker, cost per 1k tokens).
- For the routing policy: propose we codify two explicit routes for the pilot — "fast-path" (quantized medium model, aggressive batching, prefix caching) and "accuracy-path" (full model, no batching, reranker stage). We’ll measure p95 latency and cost delta.

Marcus, Laura — can you own the tech notes below and drop sample config snippets by EOD?
- SDK quickstart (Node + Python) w/ sample auth flow (short-lived JWTs).
- Example routing policy JSON with TTL-based region routing and fallback order.

Avery — can you confirm whether RapidCharge will accept short-lived test credentials with read-only embeddings scope for the pilot?

One more: I'll draft a mutually agreed staged rollout: pilot (2 weeks), extended pilot (4–6 weeks w/ reranker tuning), production (SLA + reserved capacity).

-Rishi
Director, Sales | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

Thanks Irene — that aligns with our notes. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- Test creds: yes, read-only embeddings scope + generation sandbox creds are fine for staging. We want to keep production keys behind our KMS; for pilot, short-lived tokens are OK.
- Traffic profile (staging): ~15 RPS peak, avg 120 tokens per request. Production target: 180 RPS (Q4), avg 150 tokens.
- KB sample attached (small exports) and the initial answers to your security questionnaire.

On routing policy: we like Rishi’s two-route idea. One addition: please include a region-aware rule that pins EU traffic to eu-region models and only falls back to us-region if capacity is exhausted (we’ll need the auditability for GDPR).

We reviewed the SOW draft quickly and added a few redlines — I attached an annotated copy. Samir will follow up on timeline constraints from infra.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the workshop.

Cheers,

Subject: Re: RapidCharge discovery — integration recap & proposed next steps

Thanks Avery — uploading the items helps. A few quick technical commitments from the infra/SDK side: 

1) SDK + Auth
- We’ll ship Node + Python examples that illustrate short-lived JWT exchange via your IdP (or our token broker). Example flow and a sandbox script included in the Drive folder below.
- Test creds for staging: we’ll create a role-limited token (embeddings:read, generate:sandbox) with a 12-hour TTL.

2) Routing policy (pilot config) — rough snippet (we'll push actual JSON to the Drive):
- route "fast-path": model=rc-quant-med, max_batch=32, prefix_cache=true, target_p95=200ms
- route "accuracy-path": model=rc-large-fp, max_batch=1, reranker=rc-cross-enc, target_p95=450ms
- fallback: fast-path -> accuracy-path -> us-remote-hosted (cross-region)
- region pin: if request.origin.region == "eu" then prefer eu-models and only cascade to us on capacity_exhaustion=true

3) Embeddings + reranker
- We'll provide an indexer script you can run in your VPC (or we can host with encrypted storage). Reranker will be a separate cross-encoder call after candidate retrieval; we recommend starting with a kd-tree-ish recall at 100 candidates and reranking to top 5.

I pushed detailed examples and a concise pilot config to: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRC-integration-specs

Marcus — can you add the sample routing-policy JSON + canary rollout snippet by EOD? I’ll also add a short checklist for SOC 2 artifact collection.

-Laura

Avery / Samir —

Thanks for the quick replies and the artifacts. Finalized, consolidated next steps from our side and the timeline: 

Immediate (this week)
- Redwood: push SDK quickstart (Node + Python) + test creds to staging (Laura) — ETA: today EOD.
- Redwood: add sample routing-policy JSON + canary rollout snippet (Marcus) — ETA: today EOD.
- RapidCharge: confirm acceptance of test creds and share any IdP details if you want the token exchange integrated (Avery) — ETA: Mon EOD.

Pilot (2 weeks)
- Deploy fast-path + accuracy-path routing policy in staging. Measure p95 and cost per 1k.
- Tune reranker thresholds (start with confidence threshold = 0.65).
- Evaluate prefix caching ratio and KV cache hit-rate to lower cost.

Extended pilot / production prep (4–6 weeks)
- Add reserved capacity (Dedicated) if p95 SLAs require guaranteed GPU availability.
- Finalize SOW and procurement; expecting signatures to start reserved capacity provisioning.
- SOC 2 artifacts: we’ll collect audit logs and retention policy doc during this phase.

Workshop: Laura has proposed slots Tue/Wed next week 10:00–11:00 PT — I’ll send the calendar invite; please confirm which day works.

Open questions (for RapidCharge):
- Which IdP do you want to use for short-lived tokens (Okta/Azure AD/Custom)?
- Do you prefer embeddings hosted by Redwood (encrypted at rest) or running the index inside your VPC? (affects latency/cost tradeoffs)
- Any mandatory legal/security wording to include in the SOW (data residency clauses)?

I attached the revised SOW with a few minor clarifications; Samir, please flag timing constraints if any.

Thanks — looking forward to the workshop and pilot kickoff.

Best,
Irene
